The ammine ligands (NH3) are neutral, and the chloride ligands (Cl) have a charge of -1 each. Since the complex is neutral, the sum of the oxidation states of all the components must be zero. Therefore, I will calculate the oxidation number of platinum (Pt) by setting up an equation where the sum of the oxidation numbers is zero.

\[ \text{Oxidation number of Pt} + 2 \times 0 + 4 \times (-1) = 0 \]

\[ \text{Oxidation number of Pt} - 4 = 0 \]

Solving for the oxidation number of Pt gives:

\[ \text{Oxidation number of Pt} = +4 \]

Thus, the oxidation number of the metal in the compound is +4.
